questions.q: In this lab's scenario, what is the report's real query shape, once the vague complaint is translated into a concrete condition?
options: assignment_group equals a specific group, combined with opened_at falling within a 90-day window
A single filter on the record's sys_id only
A sort on the short_description field alone
No filter at all — it returns the entire table every time
questions.explain: The report's real condition is two fields combined, which is exactly what needs to be checked against the table's indexing.

questions.q: What pattern in the report's history points to a full table scan as the likely cause?
options: A steady decline in speed that tracks the table's growing row count, rather than a sudden one-time spike
The report failing with an error message every time it runs
The report only being slow for one specific user
The report returning zero results instead of running slowly
questions.explain: A full scan's cost scales directly with row count, so a query that was fast and has steadily slowed as the table grew is the tell-tale signature.

questions.q: Why isn't an index on assignment_group alone enough to fully cover this report's query?
options: The report filters on assignment_group and a date range together, so a single-field index still leaves each matching row's date checked individually
ServiceNow doesn't allow indexes on the assignment_group field
Single-field indexes are always slower than no index at all
The opened_at field cannot be indexed under any circumstances
questions.explain: A composite index across both fields is what covers the query's real combined condition in a single step, which a single-field index cannot do.

questions.q: What real cost does the lab weigh against adding the composite index?
options: The incident table is written to constantly, so one more index adds overhead to every future insert and update on that table
Composite indexes are illegal under ServiceNow's platform licensing
Adding an index would delete existing Incident records
There is no real cost to adding any index, ever
questions.explain: Indexes speed up reads but slow down writes, and incident is one of the most heavily written tables in a typical instance.

questions.q: Why does the lab conclude this particular composite index is justified, rather than rejecting it purely on write-cost grounds?
options: The problem is a recurring, stakeholder-visible report that will keep worsening as the table grows, so the read benefit outweighs the added write cost
Write cost never actually matters on any ServiceNow table
The report in question is run only once a year, so any fix is automatically worth it
ServiceNow Support requires every slow report to get an index regardless of cost
questions.explain: The recommendation weighs this specific, real, worsening problem against the real write cost — not a blanket rule to index everything.
